parameters.content:
## Credentials Expiry Review
**00:00 and 12:00 Europe/Madrid.** Lists every credential through the n8n public API, then answers the only question that matters for each: *is it still alive, and when does it die?*

**Alive** - one probe node per expirable type (`probe_linkedin`, `probe_gmail`, `probe_google_sheets`) makes a real request to the provider with that credential. This is the only mechanism that detects an expired token: no n8n endpoint exposes an expiry, and n8n's own test for OAuth types only checks that an access token is *stored*, so a token dead for months still answers OK.

**When** - read from the credential's own name (`GitHub PAT (expires 2026-08-01)`, `caduca 15/09/2026`), or derived from `type_lifetime_days` for a type with a fixed lifetime and no refresh. No credential list is kept in the repo.

Probe evidence outranks dates **both ways**: a rejected token is EXPIRED whatever its name says, and a token that still answers is not expired just because a derived date ran out. 403/404 count as alive (the request authenticated first); 429/5xx are inconclusive and stay silent.

Only the three types above can expire in this instance - everything else is a plain API key, valid until revoked, which is not a date. Silent when nothing needs a reaction.

## Live credential test
`test_credentials` calls `POST /credentials/{id}/test` per credential and reads `{status, message}` off the response. **That endpoint answers in two different ways**, and the difference matters more than the status does:

**Real check** - a credential type with its own `test` block (most API-key types: slack, github, n8n itself) triggers an HTTP call to the provider with response rules. `OK` here means the key genuinely still works.

**Presence check** - a type descending from `oAuth2Api` (linkedIn, gmail, googleSheets) gets `oauth2CredTest`, which is only `'access_token' in oauthTokenData`. No provider call. A token that died months ago still answers `OK`, so this can never detect an expired OAuth token - only one that was never connected.

`evaluate_expiry` labels the two apart and the digest reports them on separate counters, because reporting a presence check as a verified credential is how a dashboard lies.

A response with no `status` at all (403 from a missing `credential:read` scope, timeout) counts as *not checked* rather than healthy.

nodes.name: schedule_trigger
nodes.notes: 00:00 and 12:00 Europe/Madrid (settings.timezone). Twice a day because the probes detect a token that died since the last run - a 12-hour blind spot is the most a workflow can be broken before someone hears about it.

nodes.name: set_workflow_vars
nodes.notes: N8N_API_URL is not set on the n8n pod, so the fallback is the in-cluster service. It has to be the internal URL: the public host routes /api/ through oauth2-proxy, which would answer the API call with a login page.

nodes.name: download_expiry_config
nodes.notes: DownloadTemplate reads the file from GitHub (datahub-local-ai, main branch), so registry edits only take effect once committed and pushed.

nodes.name: list_credentials
nodes.notes: GET /api/v1/credentials. Owner/admin API key required (credential:list scope). Returns id, name, type, createdAt, updatedAt and sharing - never the credential data itself.

nodes.name: filter_testable
nodes.notes: Picks what to test via test_type_patterns (default: everything). alwaysOutputData is required: an empty result would stop the chain and with it the digest, so the empty item it emits costs one harmless 404 that evaluate_expiry discards.

nodes.name: test_credentials
nodes.notes: POST /credentials/{id}/test per expirable credential. fullResponse keeps the HTTP status, so a 403 from a missing credential:read scope is distinguishable from a real 'Error' verdict - without it, an unauthorised run would look like every credential passing.

nodes.name: probe_linkedin
nodes.notes: Real call to LinkedIn with the stored token - the only way to learn a 60-day token died, since n8n's own test only checks that a token is stored. executeOnce keeps it to one request no matter how many credentials came down the chain. 401/invalid_grant = expired; 403 = authenticated but the credential lacks the openid/profile scope, which still proves the token is alive.

nodes.name: probe_gmail
nodes.notes: Google refresh tokens die when revoked, when the account password changes, or 7 days after issue while the OAuth app is still in Testing mode. A failed refresh surfaces here as invalid_grant, which no date-based check could ever see.

nodes.name: probe_google_sheets
nodes.notes: Drive `about` rather than a spreadsheet read, so no spreadsheet id has to be hardcoded. A 403 for a narrow scope still counts as alive - the refresh succeeded before Google ever looked at the scope.

nodes.name: no_notification
nodes.notes: Nothing is expiring and notify_when_clean is false, so the run ends here rather than posting a message nobody has to act on.
